framework: ICO Guidance on AI and Data Protection
title: Data protection-compliant AI development and deployment
text: Apply UK GDPR principles to AI systems processing personal data, including lawful basis, transparency, and safeguards. For LLM systems, document what data is processed and why, and design retention/access controls. Maintain evidence that privacy decisions are operational and reviewed.

framework: ICO Guidance on AI and Data Protection
title: Fairness expectations and bias risk handling
text: Consider fairness impacts of AI processing and decision-making and manage bias risks. Define fairness objectives, evaluation datasets, and mitigation steps. Fairness work should be documented as a decision trace: assumptions, tests, findings, actions.

framework: ICO Guidance on AI and Data Protection
title: Transparency and explainability for individuals
text: Provide meaningful information about AI processing and decisions to affected individuals. For chatbot interactions, disclose AI involvement, limitations, and escalation routes. Explainability should help individuals understand how outcomes were produced and what they can do next.

framework: UK Code of Practice for the Cyber Security of AI
title: Cybersecurity controls for AI systems
text: Adopt secure development and operational practices for AI systems, including threat modeling and vulnerability management. Address AI-specific attack surfaces such as prompt injection and model extraction. Maintain monitoring and incident runbooks that produce explainable response narratives.

framework: UK Code of Practice for the Cyber Security of AI
title: Threat modeling for AI-specific attack surfaces
text: Identify AI-specific threats (prompt injection, data poisoning, model inversion/extraction) and map mitigations to each lifecycle stage. Define detection signals and response actions. Threat models should be revisited as the system and attackers evolve.

title: Regulator resource hub as governance baseline
text: Use regulator guidance as a baseline for practical controls and governance expectations. Track updates and translate them into operational changes (policies, controls, training). This supports explainable alignment rather than ad-hoc interpretation.
